AWPTCM-T33249.objective:
• Enabling "arp log" causes ARP creation, aging timeout, static ARP create, static ARP delete, and ARP movement events to be logged to the system log.
  • MAC addresses appear in ARP log messages using the format selected by the mac-address-format setting (default dotted-hexadecimal or IEEE colon-separated).
  • The "arp log" command (including the mac-address-format ieee option) is accepted by the CLI and the configuration is stored correctly.
  • ARP logging configuration present in the startup configuration causes ARP events to be logged after device startup or reload.
  • The "no arp log" command removes the logging configuration and stops logging of ARP events.
  • ARP log messages are generated and visible via terminal monitor and show log commands with accurate event and address details.

steps.description: Note: Related ART Tests linked in Traceability.
Enable "arp log" (with and without mac-address-format ieee). Generate dynamic ARP entries via traffic. Confirm creation events are logged with MAC addresses in the selected format.
Allow dynamic ARP entries to age out. Confirm aging/timeout events are logged correctly.
Create and delete static ARP entries. Confirm both create and delete events are logged.
Induce an ARP movement (IP address associated with a new MAC). Confirm a movement event is logged.
Save the arp log configuration to startup-config. Reload or restart the device. Confirm ARP events continue to be logged after startup.
Disable ARP logging using the "no arp log" command. Generate ARP activity and confirm no further ARP log messages are produced.
Verify that show log and terminal monitor display the ARP log messages, and that the mac-address-format setting correctly controls the displayed address format.
